rule_citation: Va. Code § 56-594 (IOU net metering); § 56-594.01 (electric cooperative net metering); 20VAC5-315 (Net Energy Metering regs); 20VAC5-314 (Interconnection of Small Electrical Generators)
applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni, but co-ops operate under separate § 56-594.01 program with their own caps, and municipal utilities (e.g. Danville, Harrisonburg, Manassas) are not subject to SCC jurisdiction and set their own net metering policy by local ordinance/utility commission action
nem_successor: Not closed; Dominion Energy Virginia customers interconnecting after the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order in Case No. PUR-2025-00079 move to a new 'NEM 2.0' tariff that keeps 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting, but changes the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate to $0.05829/kWh (previously avoided cost, ~3.5c/kWh) and adds a $1/month admin fee; all pre-order Dominion NEM customers are grandfathered indefinitely on legacy terms. APCo's parallel NEM case was decided in the utility's favor (no material changes) in Sept. 2025. Dominion required to file revised tariffs within 90 days of the 4/30/2026 order (~by 7/29/2026).
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC (IOU default under § 56-594; co-op default is 20 kW AC per § 56-594.01 program, varies slightly by co-op rider)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 3 MW (statutory cap under § 56-594 for nonresidential eligible customer-generators; individual IOU tariffs may set lower nonresidential program sub-caps, e.g. Dominion caps at 1 MW)
nem_aggregate_cap: 6% of each utility's prior-year peak load (raised from 1% by the 2020 Virginia Clean Economy Act), with 1 percentage point of the 6% reserved for low-income program participants; as of 2026 SCC filings, Dominion and APCo both report participation well under the 6% cap statewide, though specific co-op sub-caps are much closer to full in some territories (see utility file for local subscription levels)
nem_sizing_rule: System generating capacity may not exceed expected annual energy consumption based on the customer's own usage history (no fixed % sizing rule; utility discretion to verify via 12-month billing history)
export_credit_value: 1:1 retail credit throughout the year for both IOUs and co-ops; Dominion year-end net-excess-generation cash-out is $0.05829/kWh effective for NEM 2.0 customers per the April 30, 2026 SCC order (legacy Dominion customers retain avoided-cost cash-out, historically ~3.5c/kWh); APCo year-end excess purchased at avoided cost (~3.5c/kWh, 2019 figure, last published)
credit_rollover: indefinite monthly rollover within the annual period
annual_true_up: Annual true-up date varies by utility (typically customer's April/anniversary billing cycle); excess above what's used in the true-up period is cashed out at avoided cost (APCo, legacy Dominion) or $0.05829/kWh (Dominion NEM 2.0, new interconnections)
ic_fast_track_kw: Not explicitly tiered as 'fast track' in 20VAC5-314; Level 1 process covers inverter-based systems meeting UL 1741-SB certification requirements
ic_simplified_kw: Level 1 threshold effectively covers most residential/small C&I systems (see ic_application_fee tiers); Level 2/3 required for larger or non-certified systems
ic_application_fee: $100 (Level 1 processing fee); $1,000 (Levels 2 and 3 processing fee); $500 nonrefundable fee for a pre-application report; up to $50 inverter-settings inspection fee
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2/3 review triggers for systems not qualifying for Level 1 (generally above small inverter-certified systems; SGF regulation covers systems up to 500 kW)
external_disconnect: Utility discretion (readily accessible, lockable, visible disconnect commonly required by utility interconnection agreements; not uniformly mandated in statute for all inverter-based systems)
insurance_required: Yes — liability insurance required, historically $100,000 for systems <=10 kW and $300,000 for systems >10-20 kW (co-op figures; IOU requirements similar order of magnitude, confirm per utility)
ic_timeline_days: Not codified as a fixed statewide day-count in the reviewed sources; utilities target order-of-weeks for Level 1 inverter-certified systems
non_export_option: Yes — non-export/limited-export interconnection paths exist for larger systems seeking to avoid full interconnection studies, per utility TIIR/interconnection procedures (utility-specific; not detailed in state-level source reviewed)
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (not explicitly addressed in state-level sources reviewed; utility practice may vary — see utility file and storage_specific_notes)
standby_charge: Yes — SCC-authorized standby charge for net-metered residential customers of Dominion Energy Virginia above the AC capacity threshold
standby_threshold_kw: 20 kW AC effective July 1, 2026 under HB 1255 (raised from 15 kW AC, which itself succeeded the original 10 kW AC threshold set in 2011 under HB 1983); threshold applies to aggregate nameplate AC capacity of the customer's generating facility as stated on interconnection paperwork, not actual production

rule_citation: W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 (net metering and interconnection standards); 150 CSR 33 (Rules Governing Electric Utility Net Metering Arrangements and Interconnections)
applies_to: All utilities offering net metering (IOU, municipal utilities serving >=30,000 customers, and rural electric cooperatives are all contemplated by statute; the PSC 'shall consider adopting' a rule extending net metering to smaller munis/co-ops, so smaller munis/co-ops may not be obligated to offer it — confirm per utility)
nem_successor: Net billing (fixed volumetric export rate) has replaced 1:1 retail crediting for NEW net metering customers of Appalachian Power Co. and Wheeling Power Co. following the PSC's August 2025 rate case order; new AEP-WV enrollees after an extended grandfathering window (application submitted after 2/28/2026) receive a fixed export credit of approximately 12.4 cents/kWh (67-75% of full retail rate) instead of 1:1. Separately, Monongahela Power and Potomac Edison (FirstEnergy) customers who interconnect on/after 1/1/2025 receive fixed rates of 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), or 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation) per the 2024 PSC-approved settlement (effective 3/27/2024); existing (legacy/grandfathered) customers of all four IOUs remain on 1:1 full retail net metering, with Mon Power/Potomac Edison legacy customers explicitly grandfathered for 25 years from the settlement date.
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC (statewide statutory/PSC-rule cap for residential, per W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 and Level 1 interconnection definition in 150 CSR 33 / AEP TIIR)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 500 kW (commercial cap per current AEP/FirstEnergy tariffs, consistent with § 24-2F-8(f) directive that PSC consider raising commercial cap to 500 kW); 2 MW (industrial cap per current AEP/FirstEnergy tariffs, consistent with § 24-2F-8(f) directive re: industrial cap up to 2 MW)
nem_aggregate_cap: 3% of each electric utility's aggregate customer peak demand in West Virginia during the previous year, with no less than 0.5% of that reserved specifically for residential customer-generators (W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8(g)); current subscription level as a % of the cap not published in sources reviewed
nem_sizing_rule: No fixed statewide sizing percentage found in statute or PSC rule reviewed; utility interconnection agreements govern via nameplate AC capacity caps rather than a load-based sizing formula
export_credit_basis: Mixed — 1:1 retail (legacy/grandfathered customers, all four IOUs) or fixed volumetric export rate (new customers post-reform)
export_credit_value: Legacy/grandfathered: 1:1 retail. New AEP-WV (Appalachian Power, Wheeling Power) customers after grandfathering window closes: ~12.4 cents/kWh (PSC order, Aug. 2025). New Mon Power/Potomac Edison customers on/after 1/1/2025: 9.34c/kWh (residential/schools/churches/general service), 9.15c/kWh (large general service), 8.91c/kWh (large power/alternative generation) — rates fixed for 2025-2026 per 2024 settlement, subject to renegotiation in the companies' 2026 ENEC case.
credit_rollover: Indefinite for legacy 1:1 customers (grandfathered 25 years from interconnection/settlement date for Mon Power/Potomac Edison); monthly/annual treatment for new fixed-rate customers not fully detailed in sources reviewed
annual_true_up: Excess credited against the energy portion of the bill only (not fixed/demand charges) for Mon Power/Potomac Edison per 2024 settlement; AEP-WV true-up treatment for new fixed-rate customers not fully detailed in sources reviewed
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (with IEEE 1547.1 testing protocols) + UL 1741-SB (per AEP WV Net Metering Customer Information Guide v2.0, eff. 2/1/2026)
ic_fast_track_kw: Level 1: nameplate capacity <=25 kW, inverter-based, non-islanding, UL-listed/certified per Appendix C of 150 CSR 33, interconnecting at <=69kV
ic_simplified_kw: Level 1 threshold effectively serves as the simplified/fast-track tier (<=25 kW)
ic_application_fee: $30 (Level 1); $50 + $1/kW of capacity (Level 2, i.e. any system not qualifying for Level 1)
ic_study_trigger_kw: Level 2 interconnection required for any system not meeting Level 1 criteria (effectively >25 kW or non-conforming equipment)
external_disconnect: Required — labeled, lockable, visible load-break disconnect required outside near the utility meter (per AEP WV TIIR)
insurance_required: Yes — minimum $100,000 general liability insurance required while interconnected
ic_timeline_days: Not codified as a fixed statutory day-count in sources reviewed; AEP process includes 10-business-day review windows at multiple steps (test results, submittal review, meter installation)
non_export_option: Unclear — not detailed in state-level statute or PSC rule sources reviewed; utility TIIR documents may define non-export paths for larger systems (see utility file)
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (not addressed in state-level sources reviewed)
standby_charge: No statewide standby charge identified in W. Va. Code § 24-2F-8 or 150 CSR 33 as reviewed; utilities have not been found to assess a distinct 'standby charge' analogous to Virginia's — the 2025 AEP-WV net-metering reform instead restructured the ongoing export credit rate itself rather than adding a separate demand-based standby fee
